Unlike some, I find the new app less usable. For my most common use-case with my phone -- entering transactions on the road (one I believe most users will be doing more often than actually budgeting)-- it's a downgrade.   In the previous version, I clicked on a category, reviewed how much I had to spend in that category, then added a transaction and could see immediately the effect it had on the category.  In *this* new version, I have repeatedly clicked on a category first to check and then go to enter a transaction but instead realized I accidentally *rebudgeted*!  Instead, I have to back out, then search for a little teeny + on the bottom of the screen (note- I have a 6" screen on my Android Pixel XL - I can't imagine how tiny it is on any smaller screen), and  enter a transaction that's completely disconnected from any category. I "pick" a category while entering, but that doesn't show me how much is available, or what the effect is of the transaction on *that* category.   I find the new [MARCA] feels *less* category-first controlled spending and more "just track transactions and figure it out later".

I've been using [APP] for years and decided to give this new, web-based version (as opposed to the old one that syncs via your own Dropbox) a try. I like that I can edit accounts and budgets from my phone anytime, instead of having to make a mental note to do from the desktop. And I think the Overspent Category adjustment feature is quite nifty. But I find some things not so user-friendly. Like the inverted numeral pad (what's wrong with the standard version that all other apps use?); the bug that auto-populates transaction fields – down to split categories – based on your last transaction, to the point you worry you're accidentally editing an old transaction;  and the fact that you have to go through so many loops to view your recent recent transactions. I've paid for [APP] 3 and 4, but I don't feel that this new web-based [APP] has unique enough features to 1) justify the monthly billing and 2) overcome the interface annoyances.

No way to specify the pay cycle. App calculates everything as "average" monthly.  And then it says I've overbudgeted because it's deducting a whole month of expenses from a single paycheck. That's annoying as heck. I'm on a 14 day pay cycle. Newsflash: I'm not going to have enough in a 14 day paycheck to meet a whole month of expenses.  Plus, different months have different numbers of paydays. And different bills hit at different times of the month.  I would gladly pay the $87 USD (Let's take a minute to absorb that number) for an App that, once programmed, helped my track my $ in/out for this pay cycle.  You know.  A budget App? Tell me which bills are going to hit before I get paid again, how much cash I need to reserve for upcoming bigger bills, and then let me know the bottom line: how much I have left (to spend or save) at the end. Bonus points if it can maintain a running tally of that bottom line until my next payday.  How hard could that be?! But this app can't do that. Just a gimmick that looks fancy and doesn't do anything useful.  Keep looking broke peeps.
